request: How does Bayesian optimization decide which setting to try next?

composition.story: Bayesian optimization builds a probabilistic surrogate model from evaluated points. It then uses an acquisition function to balance exploring uncertain regions and exploiting known high performers, picking the next sample where utility peaks.

aha.observation: The acquisition function peaks at an unexplored region with high model uncertainty, directing the next test.

states.label: Fit Surrogate
states.sentence: A Gaussian Process fits the observed evaluations.
states.why: Provides a smooth probabilistic estimate across the whole space.

states.label: Estimate Variance
states.sentence: Model uncertainty remains high far from tested points.
states.why: Quantifies ignorance to guide safe exploration.

states.label: Compute Acquisition
states.sentence: Expected Improvement combines predicted mean and variance.
states.why: Balances exploitation of good areas with exploration of unknowns.

states.label: Select Next
states.sentence: The peak of the acquisition function determines the next setting.
states.why: Maximizes expected gain per physical experiment.
